To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interweaving of heterogeneous media in everyday life and in interactive systems is an important design consideration.

(1) people can accommodate and make use of heterogeneity and seams between media; (2) this accommodation is a process of interweaving and recontextualising; (3) the interweaving is not seamless and is not necessarily invisible to users, but may be seamless and invisible to designers and researchers; (4) the interweavings are not always successful, and may be problematic, but may be made successful through seamful design.

(a) people can and will accommodate to and use heterogeneous media and devices, and that (b) the seams between heterogeneous media and devices can be designed in ways that make the seams visible and that can be used by the users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the seams and heterogeneity in interactive systems can be designed to be useful and productive for the user.
the design of systems that support and enhance the process of interweaving heterogeneous media and tools.
understanding how to design for seamful interaction in order to support the interweaving of media and activity in everyday life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the seams of heterogeneity are not only unavoidable, they are desirable and necessary, and that the design goal should be to make seams and heterogeneity more apparent and more useful to users, and to design systems that can interweave with other media and tools.
seamful interweaving is an essential part of the theory of interactive systems.
seamful interweaving is a key concept in design for interactive systems, and that it is an important and under-represented part of HCI theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design of interactive systems should be informed by a more comprehensive understanding of the interdependence of heterogeneous media, and of how people accommodate and take advantage the heterogeneity of media in and through the processes of interaction.
we are trying to understand how people use technology and how we can design it to better support them.
we have proposed that a seamful approach to design is a useful way to understand and support the interweaving of heterogeneous media in everyday activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use seams as a design tool to help users to become aware of and make sense of the heterogeneous nature of the world around them.
we should not aim for seamlessness, but instead design for seamfulness, by making seams visible and supporting their use in the context of activity.
we should design for seamful interweaving of media, not for seamless integration of media, and that the theory of HCI needs to reflect this.
